subject: System Design
title: Caches: Speed Through Memory
description: Learn Caches: Speed Through Memory in one minute.

hook.text: Reading from a database takes 5 milliseconds. Reading from cache takes 0.1 milliseconds. That's 50x faster.

buildup.text: A cache stores frequently accessed data in fast memory so the database isn't hit every time.

discovery.text: Redis and Memcached are popular caches. They sit between the application and the database.

twist.text: Cache invalidation — knowing when cached data is stale — is famously one of the hardest problems in computing.

climax.text: Caching is the single most effective way to make a slow system fast.

punchline.text: The fastest query is the one you don't make.

quiz.question: What is cache invalidation?
options: Knowing when cached data is stale and needs refreshing
